title: farsight.config.json
description: Workspace config for one Farsight source: the file at the source root speaks for the whole source; a farsight.config.json in a folder below it speaks only for the code under that folder, and every path it names is relative to that folder (projects and tooling are root-only). Docs and config augment what parsing found; they never replace it. Any other key is ignored with a note; keys starting with $ are for editors.

^\\$.description: Keys starting with $ ($schema, $comment) are for editors; Farsight skips them.

tags.description: tag → list of matchers. A node matches on substring of its path or name (case-insensitive).

additionalProperties.description: Matchers: a substring of a node's path or name.

glossary.description: node name (or `METHOD /path` for routes) → business-lens label/description. A class member (`Class.member`) matches, in order: its exact name, then its member part, then its class part.

guards.description: guard label → matchers. A function matcher (substring of path or name) turns the function into a guard node and flips calls into it to guards edges on the caller; a route matcher (`GET /api/v1/track/{token}`) declares a gate on that route.

additionalProperties.description: Matchers: a substring of a function's path or name, or a route.

entrypoints.description: entrypoint label → matchers. Matching nodes get searchable entrypoint tags so trace_flow can seed from them (cron/queue jobs…).

additionalProperties.description: Matchers: a substring of a node's path or name.

setup.description: node ids (or name matchers, the guards shape) of the functions that build the process container — the setup closure's roots.

plumbing.description: glob(s) whose functions are plumbing regardless of @business: helpers in journeys, out of the coverable set, never entry points.

design.description: Design manifests (docs/design/screens.json) describing this repo's screens. Discovery by filename still runs.

manifest.description: A repo-relative (or folder-relative, in a nested file) manifest path.

path.description: The same as manifest, the older spelling.

url.description: A manifest served at a URL.

name.description: What to call the design source.

openapi.description: OpenAPI/Swagger documents describing this repo's HTTP surface — a repo-relative path or a URL each. Discovery by filename still runs; this adds specs it would not find (e.g. served by the API itself).

url.description: A spec served at a URL.

storybook.description: the repo's Storybook(s) — where the config lives and where it runs when it runs (ADR 9). Discovery of `.storybook/main.*` still runs; this names the URL and the start command.

externals.description: third-party systems the parser cannot see by itself, or renames/kinds for ones it can.

stores.description: the data stores the repo's tables live in, when the code does not say — fills the gap, never overrides code. In a nested file a declaration names only the tables under that file's folder; the nearer file wins.

tooling.description: glob(s) of tooling — scripts a person runs by hand, not the running app. Default ["scripts/**"]; [] turns it off. Root-only.

lifecycle.description: The words people use for a record's statuses, per persona, and the conditions they see that are not a status. Keyed by the record's node id or table name. The code decides the statuses and the moves; this only names them — a status the code does not declare is a note. In a nested file an entry names only records whose statuses are declared under that file's folder; the nearer file's word stands.

label.description: The word the business lens shows.

description.description: One sentence on what it does, in plain words.

testReport.description: Where one level's results/coverage reports live. Paths are repo-relative globs; the adapter never runs tests.

results.description: per-case status/duration: a vitest `json` reporter file, a playwright `json` reporter file, or junit XML — one glob or several

coverage.description: istanbul-shaped coverage-final.json — attributed at the run level unless the report names a test; one glob or several

report.description: an html report to deep-link to — one, or one per results file

testLevel.description: one block, or one per config file that gave this level

tests.description: Test suites and the reports that observed them. Discovery by glob still runs; this adds report locations and extra spec globs.

include.description: extra globs that claim a file as a test (added to the defaults)

exclude.description: globs that un-claim a file the defaults would have taken

storybook.description: One Storybook. Farsight never starts it.

configDir.description: repo-relative `.storybook` directory; matched against the discovered ones (default: the only one found)

url.description: where it is served when it runs (`http://localhost:6006`) — the only origin the viewer will frame

root.description: repo-relative directory its `componentPath`s are relative to (default: the config dir's parent)

command.description: what a person runs to start it (`npm run storybook`) — printed when it is not reached

external.description: One declared third-party system: the client the calls go through, what to call it, and what kind of system it is.

import.description: a bare package specifier, or `<repo-relative path>::<Class>` — the client class the external is reached through

kind.description: What kind of system it is.

store.description: this external is (true) or is not (false) used as a data store — overrides the default from the kind (erp · db · files are)
One declared data store. Without `tables` it names the store of every table the code left unnamed; with `tables` it names only those (by table name). Code always wins.

kind.description: What kind of store it is.

engine.description: A database engine, when you know it.

tables.description: The table names this store holds; absent = every table the code left unnamed.

journeys.description: How the journeys are organised: personas and groups in the order they are shown, and a flow's placement by id. The root file's block applies to every manifest of the source, a nested file's to the manifests under its folder. The same shapes as a manifest's, every field but the id optional (an override gives only what it changes).

persona.description: The persona it exists under only.

id.description: The flow id a manifest declared.

persona.description: Who the flow is for: a persona id or name, or several.

order.description: Its place in the group, ascending.

items.description: A storyline override: the journeys told one after another as one story. Only the id is needed; the fields given override the manifest's storyline of that id.

description.description: One or two sentences on what the story is.

journeys.description: Flow ids, in the order the story tells them; an entry written as an object with branchOf and when is a branch off that step.

lanes.description: The lanes the swimlane layout names or overrides (a list given in config replaces the manifest's).

handoffs.description: Hand-offs the swimlane layout draws when the graph finds both ends (a list given in config replaces the manifest's).

projects.description: How the workspace's project tags group. A dimension with the prefix or the key of a default (`scope:` → domain, `type:` → type, `platform:` → platform) replaces it; any other is added. Root-only.

prefix.description: The tag prefix that gives a value under the key (`scope:`).

tagValues.description: tagValues[key][value] is the word a lens prints for a tag value.

graphFile.description: A project-graph file NX wrote (`nx graph --file=<path>.json`), source-relative. Read, never produced: Farsight does not run NX.

storylineEntry.description: One entry of a storyline's journeys written as an object. With only an id it is a step, like a bare flow id. With branchOf it is a branch: a journey a case takes only when the condition in when holds, leaving the storyline at the step branchOf names and, when rejoins names a step, coming back there. A branch is declared, never guessed from the code.

id.description: The flow id of the journey.

branchOf.description: The step of this storyline (a flow id in its journeys) the branch leaves from.

when.description: The condition that takes a case down the branch, in words. Required for a branch: one without it is a note and is not drawn.

rejoins.description: The step of this storyline the branch comes back to; leave it out when the case leaves the storyline there.

views.description: persona id → { word → the statuses (as the code spells them) that persona calls by that word }.

overlays.description: Conditions a person sees that are not a status — a row in another table.

name.description: The word a person uses for it.

table.description: The table it is read from (node id or table name); one the code does not have is a note.

storylineLane.description: One lane of the storyline's swimlane layout, named by the design. Lanes are derived from the graph — one per persona who owns a journey of the storyline and one per store its code writes to — so an entry only names, orders or adds a second line to one. Give exactly one of persona or store. An entry the graph cannot find is a note, never a lane.

id.description: The lane's id; a hand-off may name it.

persona.description: A declared persona id: the lane of that kind of person.

store.description: A store's name as the code or the config gives it: the lane of that store.

surface.description: Where that person works, a second line under the lane's name.

name.description: The word the lane is printed under, in place of the persona's or the store's.

storylineHandoff.description: A hand-off the swimlane layout draws when the graph finds both ends. Each end is a lane (its id, a persona id or a store name) or a screen written journey-id#n (the n-th screen of that journey of the storyline, from 1). kind moves: the screen moves the record into status in a store lane. kind seen: a screen in another lane reads the record in status. One the graph cannot find is a note, never an arrow.

from.description: Where the hand-off starts: a screen (journey-id#n) for moves, a store lane for seen.

to.description: Where it ends: a store lane for moves, a screen (journey-id#n) for seen.

kind.description: moves: the screen's action moves the record. seen: the screen shows the record in that status without the person doing anything.

status.description: The status as the code spells it. Required for moves; a seen hand-off without one is a note.

when.description: A label for the arrow, in words.
